Content:
I've read that Ikarian wine, an outcome of the surviving ancient recipe of storing the wine in clay jars buried in the earth, is about as close to Pramnian wine as you can get, exceedingly dry and strong.  

Pramnian wine, described as a black and austere wine, was produced on the island of Icaria, on the mount Pramnos, and was so dry and strong Athenians didn’t enjoy it.

Looking at the Ikarian wines, the Icarus Black Dry Red Fokiano seems to fit closest to the description.

There is this problem with Greeks and cereals. They are not enough. Our country and our islands is 95% mountain. There are some planes, but they are not enough for the greek population, and famines due to lack of cereals were not uncommon in the antiquity. Athenians had the biggest problem, they had to rely on the sales of wine and olives and olive oil, to have the money to buy cereals to feed their population. Most likely, cereals from Egypt that was the granary of Mediterranean. 
   Now Egyptians, had plenty cereals and could make beer. A lot of it. Greeks couldn't afford to make beer, because their cereals were precious and wine was superior anyway. Vines and olive trees are plants that like greek mountains, so Greeks had to rely on those to survive. So they had to prefer wine over beer and over any other beverage made of cereals. So the fact that they drunk such an unsavoury drink made of barley, makes no sense. Unless it was infected barley. Which is the easiest thing to get in Greece. Ergot thrives in our climate. Just grow a piece of land with barley or any other cereal and use no pesticides. It's guaranteed that you'll get ergot infested plants. So I'm pretty certain that the only reason they liked kykeon and spent their precious cereals on such a drink, was microdosing. They describe to have the same effects too.
